profile.entities: CCL Products (India) Ltd; Percol (UK); Vietnam Subsidiary
profile.subseg: Instant Coffee (Spray-dried); Freeze-dried Coffee; Retail Branded Coffee; Private Label Exports
profile.themes: Balance Sheet De-leveraging; Volume-led Growth vs Price Volatility; Premiumization (Freeze-dried mix)

deepdive.sec: Specialty Coffee Processing & Global B2B/B2C Beverages

bull_bear.body: Primary focus on debt reduction (Net Debt target ~INR 1,100-1,200cr for FY27 despite working capital needs for growth). Open to M&A if attractive opportunities arise. Dividend policy not explicitly guided for increase, but strong FCF expected to support shareholder returns after debt servicing.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Green coffee price volatility (though hedged via cost-plus). Middle East geopolitical tensions impacting freight/energy costs (managed so far). Competition in domestic branded space (discounting pressure in quick commerce). Subsidiary profit volatility due to centralized production planning and phasing of high/low margin contracts across entities.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and prudent. Emphasizes balance sheet strength and operational efficiency over aggressive expansion. Conservative guidance (15%) despite beating previous targets, citing base effects and mix normalization. Willing to act on capacity only when necessary to avoid constraining growth.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Subsidiary profit volatility is artificial due to centralized production planning and contract phasing, not fundamental business deterioration. The shift to longer-term contracts is happening specifically in the freeze-dried segment, locking in capacity utilization. Management explicitly states they will not let capacity constrain growth, hinting at potential 'capacity-as-a-service' or tie-up models rather than traditional CAPEX if demand spikes.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated, geographically diversified manufacturing network across India, Vietnam and Switzerland, improving production flexibility and supply chain resilience
- Vietnam operates as a fungible second manufacturing base, which the company leveraged to minimise disruption from US tariff/trade policy changes
- Long-standing customer relationships with leading global retailers, coffee brands and foodservice customers, reinforcing its position as a trusted supply partner
- Reach across more than 110 countries with one of the industry's most diversified private-label platforms, reinforcing leadership in private-label instant coffee
- Diversified green-coffee sourcing strategy across multiple geographies with long-standing supplier relationships, mitigating commodity price and supply-chain risk
- Expanding domestic branded business across general trade, modern trade, e-commerce and D2C channels, complementing its private-label manufacturing leadership
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price risk (green coffee) — The coffee industry remains exposed to fluctuations in green coffee prices arising from weather-related disruptions, crop yields, geopolitical developments, currency movements, and global supply-demand dynamics; sustained volatility in raw material prices may impact procurement costs and operating margins.
- Foreign exchange risk — A significant portion of revenues is generated through exports, making financial performance sensitive to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates.
- Supply chain risk — Global supply chains continue to face disruptions arising from geopolitical uncertainties, logistics constraints, transportation challenges, and evolving trade regulations, which may affect procurement and timely deliveries.
- Market competition — The global coffee industry remains highly competitive, with increasing emphasis on product innovation, quality, sustainability, and customer responsiveness.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — Operating across multiple international markets requires continuous compliance with changing regulatory, environmental, food safety, and trade requirements.
- Climate risk — Climate change, changing environmental regulations, and increasing stakeholder expectations continue to influence the global coffee value chain.
- Global trade-policy / tariff risk — Rapid changes in international trade policies, particularly those affecting the United States, created considerable uncertainty across global supply chains during the year; the Company relied on Vietnam as a fungible second manufacturing base to mitigate this.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Domestic Business: INR 650cr (FY26), of which INR 440cr is branded retail. Continental brand is #3 nationally, #2 in select regions. D2C/Online contributes 20-25% of domestic sales. Exports: ~70% FOB basis. Product Mix: Shift towards premium freeze-dried (higher margin per kg) and small packs driving efficiency.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising input costs and freight volatility squeezing unorganized players without hedging mechanisms. | CCL Products (India) Ltd | beneficiary | High | Cost-plus model and back-to-back buying insulate margins; scale allows better freight negotiation; strong balance sheet enables working capital dominance. |
| Premiumization trend in Indian coffee consumption favoring branded, freeze-dried options. | CCL Products (India) Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Well-positioned with #3 brand rank and high freeze-dried capacity, though competition from new-age D2C brands (e.g., Blue Tokai) is intensifying in the premium roasted segment. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body: CCL manufactures instant coffee and value-added coffee solutions -- including freeze-dried coffee, specialty blends, customised formulations and functional coffee products -- primarily for global retailers, coffee brands and foodservice customers under private label, alongside a growing domestic branded coffee business sold through general trade, modern trade, e-commerce and direct-to-consumer channels.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Private-label Instant Coffee (B2B/export):** freeze-dried coffee, specialty coffee blends, customised formulations, functional coffee products, value-added coffee solutions
- **Domestic Branded Coffee:** branded packaged coffee products
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Continental Coffee Private Limited — subsidiary: India; wholly owned (100%) subsidiary, acquired 31/03/2014
- CCL Food and Beverages Private Limited — subsidiary: India; wholly owned (100%) subsidiary, acquired 07/09/2022; transacts purchase of goods, rent and loans/advances with the parent
- Jayanti Pte Limited — subsidiary: Singapore; wholly owned (100%) subsidiary, acquired 21/05/2007
- Continental Coffee SA — subsidiary: Switzerland; wholly owned (100%) subsidiary, acquired 30/05/2007; manufacturing entity that sells to and purchases goods from the parent
- Ngon Coffee Company Limited — subsidiary: Vietnam; wholly owned (100%) subsidiary, acquired 03/02/2009; the largest subsidiary by turnover and profit within the group, and paid dividend income to the parent during the year
- Mukkonda Renewables Private Limited — associate: India; associate with 20.54% shareholding held through significant influence, associated/acquired 12.01.2026; yet to commence operations -- a renewable-energy vehicle
- Karafa Products Private Limited — related party: Counterparty for sale of goods and rent transactions with the Company
- Re-cog Infotechnologies Private Limited — related party: Counterparty for purchase of goods (advance payment) transactions with the Company
business.title: Group structure (profile)

business.body:
- Integrated, geographically diversified manufacturing network across India, Vietnam and Switzerland, improving production flexibility and supply chain resilience
- Vietnam operates as a fungible second manufacturing base, which the company leveraged to minimise disruption from US tariff/trade policy changes
- Long-standing customer relationships with leading global retailers, coffee brands and foodservice customers, reinforcing its position as a trusted supply partner
- Reach across more than 110 countries with one of the industry's most diversified private-label platforms, reinforcing leadership in private-label instant coffee
- Diversified green-coffee sourcing strategy across multiple geographies with long-standing supplier relationships, mitigating commodity price and supply-chain risk
- Expanding domestic branded business across general trade, modern trade, e-commerce and D2C channels, complementing its private-label manufacturing leadership
business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA per kg improved YoY despite sequential Q4 dip due to product mix (lower proportion of high-margin coffees sold in Q4 vs Q3). Margins are protected via cost-plus model and back-to-back green coffee buying. Optical margin contraction (EBITDA %) is due to higher pass-through of green coffee prices in revenue. Green coffee prices expected to soften post-Brazilian crop, which may reduce top-line growth rate but protect volumes.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: ~15% (volume-led). Margin: EBITDA growth to track volume growth (~15%), maintaining per-kg profitability. Order Inflow: Stable; shift towards longer-term contracts in freeze-dried segment. Capex: No major greenfield/brownfield capex for FY27/FY28; only maintenance capex of INR 25-35cr.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: No formal multi-year order book disclosed; business operates on rolling contracts. Management notes a structural shift towards longer-term contracts specifically for freeze-dried capacity, providing better visibility.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Domestic branded business targeting 25% volume growth; potential to double every 3 years. International brand 'Percol' (UK) expanding to new geographies beyond UK. Snack category pilot ('Malgudi') showing positive response, scaling soon. Capacity utilization at 65% annually (70% in Q4) provides 2 years of runway without major capex; optionality for strategic tie-ups or capacity leasing if growth exceeds 20%.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Manufacturing excellence: leverage production facilities across India, Vietnam and Switzerland to improve production flexibility, capacity utilisation and supply chain resilience, backed by ongoing investment in automation, process improvement and quality systems
- Innovation and product development: continuous R&D investment to expand premium, freeze-dried, customised and value-added coffee solutions
- Strategic customer partnerships: deepen long-standing relationships with leading retailers, coffee brands and foodservice customers through consistent quality, customisation and reliable supply
- Distribution and brand development: widen distribution and retail visibility for the branded coffee business across modern trade, general trade, e-commerce and direct-to-consumer channels, complementing the private-label manufacturing business
- Operational discipline: disciplined procurement, prudent capital allocation, efficient capacity utilisation and continuous cost optimisation to support sustainable profitability
- Expansion across emerging markets, particularly Africa and China, to diversify the revenue base
- Use Vietnam as a fungible second manufacturing base to navigate tariff and trade-policy disruptions (particularly US-related) with minimal customer disruption
- Exploring new growth verticals -- ready-to-drink coffee solutions, customised offerings for international retail partners, and expansion of consumer brands into new categories
- Dividend policy is governed by a formal Dividend Distribution Policy adopted under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations. The Company paid an interim dividend during the year and the Board recommended a further final dividend, together representing an increase in per-share dividend over the prior year, reflecting a stated preference for profitable and sustainable expansion (rather than growth at any cost) supported by a healthy balance sheet, prudent capital allocation and a long-term strategic perspective. Beyond dividends, capital is also reinvested via the ESOP scheme (transfers to the ESOPs outstanding account) and via approved strategic/associate investments (e.g., the renewable-energy associate).
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY26 the Company continued investing in manufacturing excellence and process innovation across its integrated production platform in India, Vietnam and Switzerland rather than announcing a new named project: it commissioned an advanced cryogenic grinding system (using liquid nitrogen for a more uniform particle-size distribution and improved blending versus conventional micro-grinding) to supplement the existing grinding system, commissioned a vapour compression refrigeration (VCR) system that replaces a steam-driven absorption refrigeration system to cut steam consumption and GHG emissions, and installed a rooftop solar power system at its Corporate Office. Capacity expansions completed in the prior year (FY25) are described as now supporting the Company's ability to meet growing customer demand and its next phase of growth, and management refers to 'the facility becoming fully integrated into operations' as strengthening supply-chain resilience, without naming the site.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for instant coffee and value-added coffee products remained resilient across developed and emerging markets, with consumers favouring premium, convenience-oriented, customised and sustainably sourced coffee
- Private-label coffee maintained healthy momentum across major retail markets as retailers continue to expand private-label portfolios, favouring diversified, scaled manufacturers
- Significant volatility in green coffee prices during the year, driven by weather-related supply disruptions and lower crop estimates in key producing regions, increased procurement and inventory-management complexity industry-wide
- Global coffee trade remained resilient with prices remaining elevated but showing some moderation from the exceptionally high levels seen in the first three quarters of FY26
- Long-term outlook for the global coffee industry remains favourable, supported by rising coffee consumption, premiumisation and sustained demand for differentiated/customised solutions, even as near-term geopolitical and macro uncertainty persists
- India's coffee consumption is evolving steadily on changing lifestyles, growing cafe culture, rising disposable incomes and expansion of modern retail, e-commerce and D2C channels, supporting the domestic branded business
- Capacity expansions completed in the previous year are now strengthening the Company's ability to meet growing customer demand and support its next phase of growth
- Climate change and supply-side constraints remain structural considerations for the industry, favouring companies with strong sourcing capability, manufacturing flexibility and global scale
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: CCL delivered strong 46% revenue growth (driven by 20% volume + coffee price inflation) and 16% EBITDA growth, while aggressively de-leveraging the balance sheet (Net Debt/EBITDA down to 1.45x). Guidance remains conservative at 15% volume/EBITDA growth for FY27, prioritizing cash flow generation and debt reduction over immediate capacity expansion, with no major capex planned for the next two years.

open.item: Company approved an investment under the Group Captive mode through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) to access approximately 7.9 MW of renewable wind and solar power, expected to be commissioned in a subsequent period.

Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 3 per equity share (150% of face value Rs 2), subject to shareholder approval at the AGM; combined with the interim dividend of Rs 2.75/share already paid, total FY26 dividend is Rs 5.75/share, a 15% increase over FY25's Rs 5/share.
Annual blended utilisation ~65% (Q4 ~70%); expected to rise to ~72-73% in FY27 (15% growth) and ~80-85% in FY28.
Consolidated average tax rate guided to be ~17% going forward.
FY27 finance cost guided to ~INR 100 crores (from INR 130 cr FY26) at ~7.5% on ~INR 1,000-1,200 cr debt.
Branded/B2C business (INR 440 cr in FY26) to keep driving ~25% volume growth going forward; targeted to roughly double every ~3 years.
Net debt cut to ~INR 1,073 cr (down >INR 750 cr YoY); FY27 gross debt guided ~INR 1,000-1,200 cr, with intent to retire debt rather than hold cash.
FY27 guidance of ~15% volume growth with EBITDA growth in the same region (~15%).
No planned big capex for next 2 years (only INR 25-35 cr maintenance capex); company good on capacity for growth aspirations.
Vending machine business targeted to reach INR 100 crore in the next 3 to 5 years (from ~INR 20-25 crore today).
Percol (UK) at ~INR 25-30 cr revenue; targeted to reach ~INR 100 crores within 2-3 years, and to be seeded in other geographies.
Management assures capacity will not constrain growth; even at 20% growth (~72,000 tons) capacity is sufficient, and would use strategic tie-ups / bought capacity if needed.
Middle East crisis flagged as a challenge (supply disruption to ME clients, higher energy/logistics cost); managed well, cost-plus + 70% FOB insulates margins, no major guidance impact expected.
Malgudi snacks pilot (100-150 stores) got good response; broader launch of some product categories expected in a couple of months.
Actively evaluating entry of own B2C brand into US and Vietnam markets; scale to be determined after seeding.

Company is exploring new growth opportunities including ready-to-drink coffee solutions, customised offerings for international retail partners, and expansion of its consumer brands into new categories.
At peak capacity utilisation (some years out), company expects ~12-13% of the global outsourced instant-coffee market.
B2C cafe format (Contico) POC with a couple of cafes and a kiosk in Hyderabad; expansion only after proof of concept established.
EU Deforestation Regulation postponed by 1 year; company working with suppliers/growers for compliance, sees it as industry challenge.
Targeting to lift wallet share on low-share clients to 20-25%; adds ~10-15 new clients/year (4-5 drop off).

verdicts.note: Aggressive branded growth continued: FY26 brand 'INR440 crores'; 'volume was around 25%, 30%, and then... another 15%, 20% of value growth'; 'committed to driving 25% kind of volume growth' next year.

verdicts.item: Branded/B2C business (INR ~300 cr this year) targeted to double in ~3-4 years.

verdicts.item: Total capacity (~37,000 tons in FY24, ~75,000-77,000 after expansion) to be doubled to ~70,000+ MT in 4-5 years via 15-20% volume growth.

verdicts.item: EBITDA per kg to stay broadly stable (~INR 110) for next 1-2 years; Q2 uplift (from high-value contracts + ~INR 5-6 cr RoDTEP) not expected to be the new base.
verdicts.note: Per-kg sustained above the ~110 base: 'on an annual basis, in fact, the EBITDA per kilo has improved from previous year' - the uplift proved durable.

wtt.summary: 68% guidance hit (20 chains); 5/9 projects on-time; 2 expired; 23% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident on record FY26 and clean balance sheet; candid that the ~30% FY26 EBITDA growth won't repeat (freeze-dried mix & efficiencies now in base), guiding to ~15% for FY27.
